overview: The Netherlands is a country in north-western Europe on the North Sea. Its capital is Amsterdam, although the government sits in The Hague. The Netherlands is a constitutional monarchy and was a founding member of what is now the European Union. It is famous for windmills, tulips, cycling and canals, and Rotterdam has the largest port in Europe.

geography.text: The Netherlands is extremely flat, and about a quarter of the land is below sea level. Much of it has been won from the sea and lakes and is protected by dykes, dunes and pumps; this reclaimed land is called polder. The Rhine, the Maas and the Scheldt reach the sea through its delta, and the only real hills are in the far south-east.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mild, windy and wet, with cool summers and mild winters.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: The Wadden Sea, shared with Germany and Denmark, has seals and millions of migrating birds.

history.text: In 1581 the northern provinces of the Low Countries declared independence from Spain, and in the 1600s the Dutch Republic became a great trading power, in a 'Golden Age' of artists such as Rembrandt and Vermeer. The kingdom was created in 1815. The Netherlands was occupied by Germany in the Second World War, and after the deadly flood of 1953 it built huge sea defences.

events.title: Independence from Spain
events.text: The northern provinces declare independence from the Spanish king.

events.title: Dutch East India Company
events.text: A trading company is founded that builds an empire in the East Indies.

events.title: Kingdom
events.text: The Kingdom of the Netherlands is created.

events.title: German invasion
events.text: Germany invades and occupies the Netherlands.

events.title: North Sea flood
events.text: A storm surge kills more than 1,800 people, leading to the Delta Works sea defences.

government.text: The Netherlands is a constitutional monarchy, with a king as head of state and a Prime Minister leading the government. Its parliament, the States General, has two chambers. Amsterdam is the capital, but the government and parliament sit in The Hague. Governments are usually coalitions of several parties.

economy.text: The Netherlands is a trading nation. Rotterdam is the largest port in Europe, and the country is the world's second-largest exporter of food after the United States, thanks to high-tech greenhouses. It is also strong in chemicals, energy, finance and technology: ASML, which makes the machines used to produce computer chips, is Dutch.

culture.text: The Netherlands has produced great painters, including Rembrandt, Vermeer and Van Gogh. About a quarter of the country lies below sea level, protected by dykes, dunes and pumps. There are more bicycles than people, and cycling is part of everyday life.

items.title: Windmills of Kinderdijk
items.text: Nineteen windmills built to pump water out of the land.

items.title: Van Gogh
items.text: His paintings hang in the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam.

items.title: Tulips
items.text: Tulips came from Türkiye; in 1637 their bulbs sold for fortunes.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Cheese such as Gouda and Edam, herring eaten raw with onions, and stroopwafels, syrup waffles.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: The Dutch Golden Age gave the world Rembrandt and Vermeer, and Van Gogh is the most famous Dutch painter of all.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: On King's Day, 27 April, the whole country dresses in orange and holds street markets.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. The Dutch men's team has reached three World Cup finals and won Euro 1988, and its 'total football' style changed the game. The Netherlands also dominates speed skating and field hockey.

items.title: Euro 1988
items.text: The Netherlands' only major men's title.

items.title: Speed skating
items.text: The most successful nation in Olympic speed skating.

didYouKnow: About a quarter of the Netherlands is below sea level.
The Dutch are the tallest people in the world on average.

keyPeople.name: Vincent van Gogh
keyPeople.text: Painted The Starry Night; sold very few paintings in his lifetime.

keyPeople.name: Anne Frank
keyPeople.text: Her diary, written while hiding in Amsterdam, is read worldwide.
